The extruder switching system operates through a switching motor and transmission mechanism that drives the Extruder Switch Cam. This action causes the left and right driven wheel linkages (driven rods) to swing. A tension spring, attached to the driven rod, ensures that one driven wheel is pressed firmly against the drive wheel, enabling filament extrusion as the drive wheel rotates. Simultaneously, the opposite driven wheel remains disengaged, preventing unwanted filament movement.
By reversing the drive wheel's rotation, the extruder motor can selectively engage either driven wheel, enabling seamless dual extrusion using a single drive wheel.

The AMS 2 Pro Internal Hub Unit is specially designed for Bambu AMS 2 Pro, which is located at the rear of AMS 2 Pro and consists of four Hall sensors, a magnetic rotary encoder, and a motor. It merges four filament slots into one and is used to select particular filaments in AMS 2 Pro and convey filaments from AMS 2 Pro to the printer. The Hall sensor detects when the filament reaches a specific position and activates the brushless motor to provide an additional driving force for feeding the filament.
The 3520 AMS Internal Assist Motor is used to provide driving force for the operation of the AMS 2 Pro internal hub unit.

strings.en: The Filament Cutter Stopper is located inside the printer chamber. It supports the cutter during operation, enabling it to cut the filament for tasks such as material changes and unloading.
The Left Side Panel is mounted on the left side of the printer when facing the front, and the Right Side Panel is mounted on the right side when facing the front.
The Extruder Filament Sensor is located in the extruder and detects both the presence of filament and the position of the filament cutter lever.
The Filament Cutter Lever holds the cutter blade and actuates it to slice the filament.
The Toolhead Rear Cover shields the rear components of the toolhead from dust and debris.

The Extruder Unit drives filament into the hotend, boosting extrusion force, minimizing slippage, and enhancing wear resistance. Paired with a robust extruder motor, it ensures reliable extrusion power.
The Extruder Unit Front Cover protects internal components from dust and debris, aids in filament alignment, and adds to the structural integrity of the extrusion system.
The Extruder Gear Assembly precisely advances and controls filament movement, ensuring smooth printing and enabling filament changes when required.
The Hotend Heating Assembly heats the hotend and uses a clamping mechanism to secure it, enabling quick removal for maintenance or replacement.
The Extruder Motor is mounted on the toolhead and drives the extruder to feed filament.
The Eddy Sensor detects whether the nozzle is covered with melted filament.
Installed inside the extruder, it is driven by the extrusion motor to transport filament to the hot end or retract it from the extruder.
The XY-axis belt tensioner with pulleys comprises idler pulleys and brackets, enabling adjustment of the belt's travel distance under spring tension.

The X-axis controls the tool head's left-right movement. Unlike the X1/P1 series' carbon rod system , the P2S adopts a smooth rod and belt structure . The hollow steel smooth rod delivers carbon rod-level performance while its smooth surface allows easier cleaning and more convenient maintenance . X-direction motion is driven by the A and B stepper motors .
The filament cutter lever on the toolhead cuts filament just above the hotend to retract old and load new filament.
The material discharge assembly is mounted above the printer liner to expel waste generated during filament swapping.
When facing the printer's front door, the right side cover is referred to as the right side panel.
The chamber temperature sensor is an NTC with a fixed bracket, installed on the inside of the printer's front beam, and is used to detect the temperature inside the printer chamber.
The eddy current coil , installed between the extruder and the hotend, is an accessory for active calibration of filament flow.
The screen rear housing is a component installed on the back of the screen. It has clips that secure the screen to the printer.

context.title: Screen Rear Housing with Hinge - P2S

strings.en: The USB port module is mounted on the printer's top for USB drive connection.
Installed on the upper part of the extruder, it functions as a sensor for detecting filaments.
A plastic cover installed on the left side of the printer to protect the AP board cover and its connecting cables.
When facing the printer's front door, the left side cover is referred to as the left side panel.
The toolhead carriage assembly consists of front and rear shells fixed on an aluminum sleeve, enabling X-axis movement via XY belt traction.
A replaceable activated-carbon filter inside the right chamber liner. It removes VOCs produced during printing.

The front glass door, made of dark gray glass, is installed on the front of the printer, offering clear visibility of it's operation and providing protection. The P2S front glass door includes a film for enhanced security.

The heatbed of a printer is a platform installed inside the printer chamber. It moves up and down along the Z-axis and is heated to a set temperature. Setting the appropriate heatbed temperature can effectively improve adhesion between the model and the build plate while helping to prevent warping.

The left LED light strip is mounted on the AP board cover to illuminate the printer chamber. The front LED light is installed inside the front cover and provides supplementary lighting for the printer chamber.
The Z-axis stepper motor drives the heatbed along the Z-axis via a synchronous belt, and comes with a motor cable and drive pulley.
The front door sensor is a small circuit board mounted on the inside of the front column of the printer to sense the opened or closed status of the glass front door of the P2S

The XY stepper motors are mounted at the back of the printer, driving the toolhead for XY-axis movement. There is one on each side (left/right), designated as the A motor and B motor for positional differentiation.

The 3508 extruder servo motor used in the P2S is a high-precision servo motor developed by Bambu Lab. It accurately controls filament feeding, stopping, and retraction, making it a key component for ensuring print quality and success.
A central plastic housing with magnets for front cover attachment.
A plastic enclosure designed to seal the rear part of the toolhead.
A component installed on the right side of the printer chamber that switches the air circulation mode and helps cool the components.
The drag chain is a mechanical device mounted between the tool head and the rear of the printer, designed to manage and protect the tool head cables and material tubes.
The PTFE tube bracket is mounted on the back of the P2S to provide secure attachment of the PTFE tube (also known as a Bowden tube) which provides a low friction path for filament into the printer.
The P2S printer features a 5-inch touchscreen for controlling the printer and monitoring its status.

The live camera , installed inside the printer, enables real-time monitoring of the printing process via Bambu Studio and Bambu Handy . It also provides intelligent detection features such as stringing detection , foreign object detection , print bed detection , and hotend type recognition .
A plastic bracket mounted on the back of the printer to hold an external filament spool
PTFE Tube Connector: A connector used to connect the PTFE tube to the filament spool.

context.title: PTFE Tube Connector for Spool Holder - P2S

strings.en: The glass front door of the P2S swings on a top and a bottom hinge, and is mounted to each via two screws. The hinges themselves are also removable from the P2S frame.
An accessory installed on the toolhead, responsible for heating the printing materials to a molten state.
The outer shell of the extruder

context.title: Extruder Unit Front Cover Assembly - P2S

strings.en: The nozzle wiping pad is installed on the nozzle wiper part of the purge wiper and is used to remove residual waste on the nozzle. It is made of soft silicone material to ensure good contact with the hotend during wiping. Replace the nozzle wiping pad if it is damaged or detached.
An idler pulley or idler is a smooth or toothed free-spinning pulley mounted on a bearing that redirects or tensions the timing belts driving the core-XY motion system of the P2S.

The Application Processor Main Board, or AP Board for short, is the circuit board that manages all internal communication and system-level processing for the printer. It provides an independent operating environment—handling things like memory management, firmware operations, graphics processing, multimedia decoding, Wi-Fi, camera signals, LEDs, and the user interface.
The P2S uses two XY belts, each 1444 mm in length and 7 mm wide. They connect the XY motors to the toolhead and drive its movement along the XY plane.
The MC board, or Main Control Board, is a printed circuit board with integrated microprocessors, various driver chips, connectors and circuits used to operate the various aspects of the P2S.
Cools the upper part of the hotend to prevent the filament from softening prematurely and causing blockages.
The front cover of the P2S printer is a dark grey panel installed on the front of the printer, with the model number "P2S" printed on it.
The filament buffer is a special component installed on the back of the printer to reduce tension fluctuations during the feeding process and ensure smooth filament feeding.

The power switch assembly, located on the back of the printer, consists of a power cord socket, a switch that controls the printer’s power, and cables that connect the printer's power supply, AC power board, and ground wire.
The 5-inch touch screen is connected to the AP board via a Flexible Printed Circuit (FPC) ribbon cable.
